description: PRD-61: NL2SQL v2 Competitive Upgrade — Close critical gaps vs top open-source NL2SQL projects (Vanna, Dataherald, DB-GPT). 8 phases: (1) RAG-based few-shot example retrieval, (2) SQL error self-correction loop, (3) Explicit schema linking stage, (4) 5 bug fixes from code audit, (5) Golden SQL training system with UI, (6) Query confidence scoring, (7) MCP server exposure, (8) Benchmarking & monitoring. Adopt techniques (not codebases) from competitors. Takes Automatos from 'good internal tool' to 'competitive with Vanna/Dataherald' level.

Create orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/training/example_store.py with SQLExampleStore class

SQLExampleStore.get_similar_examples(question, database_source_id, limit=5, min_similarity=0.7) retrieves most similar verified examples
SQLExampleStore.mark_verified(example_id) marks an example as Golden SQL
SQLExampleStore.add_ddl(ddl, database_source_id) stores DDL for schema context retrieval

Collection name: nl2sql_examples, workspace-isolated

userStories.title: Explicit schema linking stage
userStories.description: As the system, I need a dedicated schema linking step before SQL generation that identifies the most relevant tables/columns using embeddings + semantic layer matching, replacing the brittle keyword-only _get_relevant_tables().
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/query/schema_linker.py with SchemaLinker class
SchemaLinker.link(question, schema_metadata, semantic_layer, top_k_tables=5, top_k_columns=20) returns LinkedSchema
LinkedSchema dataclass with: tables (ranked), columns (ranked), relationships, metrics matched, overall confidence score
Step 1: Semantic layer matching — map business terms to metrics/dimensions (highest priority)
Step 2: Embedding-based table ranking — score tables by similarity to question
Step 3: Column-level matching — score columns within top tables
Step 4: Relationship expansion — include JOIN bridge tables for selected tables
Replace _get_relevant_tables() call in nl2sql_service.py with schema_linker.link()
Only linked tables/columns sent to LLM prompt (40%+ token reduction)
Update orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/__init__.py to export SchemaLinker
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Bug fix: Table relevance scoring sends ALL tables
userStories.description: As a developer, the _get_relevant_tables() in nl2sql_service.py uses keyword matching only and falls back to sending ALL tables to the LLM. Fix with proper scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/query/nl2sql_service.py, replace _get_relevant_tables() with scored approach
Score factors: direct table name mention (+10), column name mention (+5), description keyword overlap (+2 per word, excluding stopwords)
Sort by score descending, take top 10
If no matches, fall back to top 5 tables by row_count (most important tables), NOT all tables
Note: This is the immediate fix; Phase 3 SchemaLinker provides the full embedding-based replacement
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Bug fix: Clarifier false positives on word boundaries
userStories.description: As a developer, the clarifier.py regex patterns match inside words — 'last_name' triggers time_range, 'baby' triggers grouping. Fix with word boundary assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/intelligence/clarifier.py, update all ambiguity_patterns to use word boundaries
time_range patterns: use \b and negative lookahead (?!_) so 'last_name' doesn't match
grouping patterns: 'by' must be followed by whitespace + word, not be part of 'baby', 'nearby', etc.
Add test cases: 'Show last_name column' should NOT trigger time_range clarification
Add test cases: 'Count babies by hospital' should NOT trigger grouping on 'baby' but SHOULD trigger on 'by hospital'
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Bug fix: Validator allows subqueries with mutations
userStories.description: As a developer, the validator.py only checks top-level for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Nested 'INSERT INTO ... SELECT' bypasses the single-statement check. Fix with recursive parsing.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/query/validator.py, update mutation checking to scan entire SQL string
Strip string literals first (replace 'content' with '' to avoid false positives on quoted keywords)
Use regex pattern matching for mutation keywords: INSERT INTO, UPDATE SET, DELETE FROM, DROP, CREATE, ALTER, TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE
Match across the full SQL including subqueries
Test: 'SELECT * FROM (INSERT INTO foo SELECT * FROM bar)' should be caught
Test: 'SELECT * FROM foo WHERE name = ''DELETE FROM bar''' should NOT be caught (it's a string literal)
Typecheck passes

If database_source_id provided, remove only cache entries for that source
If None, clear entire cache
Log cache invalidation events at INFO level
Call invalidate_cache() when schema introspection is manually triggered via API
Add /api/knowledge/sources/database/{id}/schema/refresh endpoint that triggers re-introspection + cache invalidation

userStories.title: Query confidence scoring system
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a confidence score for each generated SQL query so I know when to trust it vs review manually.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/query/confidence.py with QueryConfidenceScorer class
ScoringContext dataclass with: similar_examples, linked_schema, sql, metrics_matched, validation_clean
ConfidenceScore dataclass with: score (0-100), level (high/medium/low), factors dict, recommendation (auto_execute/review_sql/manual_review)
Factor 1 — example_match (0-30 pts): similar_count * 5 + best_similarity * 20
Factor 2 — schema_link (0-25 pts): linked_schema.confidence * 25
Factor 3 — complexity (0-20 pts): 20 minus penalties for JOINs (3 each) and subqueries (5 each)
Factor 4 — semantic (0-15 pts): metrics_used * 5
Factor 5 — validation (0-10 pts): 10 if clean, 5 if rewritten
Levels: high >= 70, medium >= 40, low < 40
Integrate scorer into orchestrator/modules/nl2sql/service.py query flow
Return confidence in query API response in orchestrator/api/database_knowledge.py
Typecheck passes
